definitions.explanation: A hole dug in the ground for burying a coffin or remains.
Used figuratively in the expression {墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る (to dig one's own grave), meaning to cause one's own downfall through careless actions or words.

examples.japanese: {墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る{作業|さぎょう}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The work of digging the grave began.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}い{墓穴|ぼけつ}に{棺|ひつぎ}が{下|お}ろされた。
examples.english: The coffin was lowered into the deep grave.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{中|なか}、{墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}り{終|お}えるまで{何時間|なんじかん}もかかった。
examples.english: It took hours to finish digging the grave in the rain.

examples.japanese: {余計|よけい}なことを{言|い}って{墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}った。
examples.english: I dug my own grave by saying something unnecessary.

examples.japanese: {嘘|うそ}をついて{墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}るな。
examples.english: Don't dig your own grave by lying.

examples.japanese: {弁明|べんめい}しようとして、かえって{墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}ってしまった。
examples.english: In trying to justify myself, I ended up digging my own grave.

notes:
USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is much more common in everyday speech than the literal sense. The expression {墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る (to dig one's own grave) is a set phrase used when someone's own words or actions lead to their downfall.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る (to dig one's own grave — literal and figurative)
- {自|みずか}ら{墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る (to dig one's own grave oneself)

RELATED WORDS:
- {墓|はか}: grave, tomb
- {自滅|じめつ}: self-destruction
- {墓地|ぼち}: cemetery
